content.text: {"primary_meaning":"The Word of God—God’s powerful, penetrating truth or speech, often portrayed as a spiritual weapon and an instrument of discernment or judgment.","primary_basis":["Ephesians 6:17 explicitly identifies “the sword of the Spirit” as “the word of God.”","Hebrews 4:12 compares the word of God to a sharp two-edged sword that penetrates and judges the heart.","Isaiah 49:2 portrays the servant’s mouth as a sharp sword.","Revelation 1:16; 2:12,16; 19:15,21 depict a sharp sword proceeding from Christ’s mouth, commonly interpreted as his authoritative word of judgment."],"alternatives":[{"meaning":"Divine judgment or punishment, including God’s judicial action against nations or evildoers.","basis":["Deuteronomy 32:41-42","Isaiah 34:5-6","Ezekiel 21:1-17","Revelation 19:15,21"],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"War, violence, death, or military destruction in a general sense.","basis":["Leviticus 26:6-8,25","Jeremiah 14:12","Ezekiel 5:12","Revelation 6:4,8"],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"Conflict, division, or the disruptive consequences of allegiance to Jesus rather than literal warfare.","basis":["Matthew 10:34-36","Luke 12:51-53"],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"The coercive and punitive authority of civil government.","basis":["Romans 13:4, where the ruler “does not bear the sword in vain”"],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"Persecution, execution, or martyrdom suffered by believers.","basis":["Romans 8:35","Hebrews 11:34,37","Revelation 13:10"],"prominence":"minority"},{"meaning":"Personal anguish or piercing sorrow.","basis":["Luke 2:35, where a sword is said to pierce Mary’s own soul"],"prominence":"minority"},{"meaning":"Illicit reliance on armed force, especially when contrasted with Jesus’ way.","basis":["Matthew 26:52","John 18:10-11"],"prominence":"minority"}],"has_settled_consensus":false,"confidence":"high","notes":"Christian teaching most recognizably uses the sword as a symbol of the Word of God, particularly in discussions of spiritual warfare. Nevertheless, biblical usage is strongly context-dependent: the sword also regularly signifies judgment, warfare, political authority, division, persecution, or sorrow. There is therefore no single settled meaning applicable to every occurrence."}
